caption: Dot 3: every pixel's place measured along a slowly turning direction - slabs of light sweeping through the cube at an angle
why: How far along a direction is this point? That one question gives slabs (measure along an axis and band it), height (measure along down), lighting (how much a surface faces a light). Dot 3 is that measurement - the dot product of two vectors.
Its neighbours: Vector math has dot among many operations; Length is distance from the origin; Dot 3 is distance along a direction.
steps: **a** is **Position**'s `pos`, the pixel's place in the cube.
**b** is a direction from **Direction to**, its heading turning with a clock (**Time** times 0.1) and tilted up 0.1.

The result is how far along that direction the pixel lies, -1.7..1.7: into a **Wave** (3 cycles), it makes flat slabs of light at right angles to the direction - and as the direction turns, the slabs sweep through the cube at a changing angle.
The wave is the **Palette**'s brightness, coloured by the same distance.

try.label: Thinner slabs
try.text: the Wave's cycles at 6: twice as many slabs, half as thick.

try.label: Tilted up
try.text: Direction to's up at 0.2: the direction tips toward vertical, so the slabs lie nearly flat - layers.
